description: Backend-developer handover manifest. Machine-readable index of front-end elements that are mock / visual-only / in-memory and need real backend implementation. Front-end-only repo (vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, no backend). See HANDOVER.md for the human-readable version and the TODO(backend:<Surface>) in-code marker convention.

categories.visual-only: Rendered but no behaviour wired at all.
categories.fe-wired: Works client-side; no backend required (may be fine as-is).
categories.needs-backend: Requires real data, API, auth, persistence, or AI service.

items.needs: POST /auth/login { email, password, remember } → establish session and redirect to the Control Centre; surface invalid-credential / field errors on the inputs (Input has an error state).

items.current: Toggles visually only.
items.needs: Bind to session lifetime on login — persistent cookie when checked, session cookie otherwise.

items.current: Links to '#'.
items.needs: Route to /auth/forgot (password-reset flow).

ControlHub.note: CC filterable directory screen. Reuses the ControlScreen app-shell (see the ControlScreen surface for all shell-level backend items — sidebar nav, auth, notifications, AI assistant, favourites, etc.). The items below are specific to ControlHub's own page content; everything else is inherited from the reused shell.

items.current: Filter field renders (search icon + clear button) but no filtering logic is wired — typing does nothing; the clear button is the component default only.
items.needs: Client-side filtering is sufficient (no backend): debounced text match over ActionCard titles across all sections, hiding cards (and empty section headings) that don't match; clear button resets. Promote to fe-wired once implemented.

items.element: .action-card--chevron (href="#") + .action-card--button (whole-card nav, pointer cursor) with a separate .btn ("+ add")
items.current: Both card variants are meant to navigate the whole card to the area's screen. Chevron cards link to '#'; Button cards show a pointer cursor but card-level navigation isn't wired; the 'add' buttons are inert.
items.needs: Real navigation targets per area for BOTH variants (whole card → the corresponding report/analysis screen — implement the Button card as a stretched-link so the '+ add' button stays a separate action above it) and an add-to-favourites/dashboard action for the 'add' button (POST, then reflect added state). Card title + section taxonomy comes from the same content source as the sidebar nav.

ControlScreen.note: CC home/landing dashboard. Front-end complete; all data is hardcoded and most actions are mock. Composes many CC patterns — see docs/component-registry.md for per-component status.

items.needs: Favourites CRUD API: GET (load on init), POST (save {name, context, timestamp}), DELETE. Replace in-memory DOM mutation with API-backed state.

items.needs: Persist pinned sub-items via a user-prefs API: GET pinned ids on init (apply --pinned on render), POST on pin, DELETE on unpin. Key by user + menu item id; share state across the desktop and mobile menu trees.

items.current: Empty inputs, no event handlers.
items.needs: Per-panel search/filter API (debounced query → results), populate the lists from the response.

items.needs: Menu/structure API to populate items; permission-based visibility; real navigation/routing on click.

items.current: Static options (Affino/Staging/etc.); selection is visual.
items.needs: Load available zones; persist selection to session; reload dashboard data for the chosen zone.

items.needs: Users API with server-side paginate/sort/search; live 'online' status (poll or WebSocket); touch/login metadata from auth.

items.needs: Mount a multi-select value picker on the filter-item:toggle event; source the option list per filter; on selection call el.setFilterValues([…]) (chip applies the 1–3 / 4+ rollup); persist the active filter set and clear via the × (filter-item:clear).

items.needs: Saved-views CRUD scoped to user+context: GET list, POST (create from current filters), PATCH (rename), POST copy, DELETE; switching a view loads its filter set.

AudioPlayer.note: Article audio player component (3 types). Playback is simulated by a JS timer so the scrubber/waveform/time read true in the demo; no real audio is bundled.

items.needs: Wire to a real <audio> element / streamed source. Contract: { src: url, duration: seconds, downloadUrl: url }. Replace the simulated ticker with audio.timeupdate; point the download button at downloadUrl.

EventBuilder.note: AI-driven event builder prototype: brief -> generated draft -> guided gap-filling -> block library -> in-context editing -> all-fields form -> published page. Front end only. The entire event model lives in the DOM and is lost on reload (bar the brief, which uses sessionStorage). Blocks map 1:1 to existing Advanced Event fields; no new event capability is implied.

items.current: Brief is typed and stashed in sessionStorage under `eb:brief`; the send button just navigates to 02.
items.needs: POST /api/event-builder/generate { brief, sectionId } -> full event model: chosen blocks + order, page shape (tabbed|scroll), first-pass field values, and a per-field confidence so the gap-fill list on 04 can be derived rather than hardcoded.

items.current: Hardcoded checklist with static done/working/pending states; the spinner is decorative.
items.needs: Stream generation events (block decided / copy written / field inferred) over SSE or websocket from the generate call, so progress reflects real work.

items.current: Three static proposals. Accept/Reject rewrite the DOM (accept clears the dashed state, reject removes the block and its rail row); nothing persists.
items.needs: Return proposals as a diff against the current event model, each with a target block, a payload and a provenance reference (e.g. 'from your 2026 page'). Accept applies the patch server-side and returns the new model; reject records the dismissal so it is not re-proposed.

items.current: Free-text prompt bar; Refine buttons pre-fill it. Submitting does nothing.
items.needs: POST /api/event-builder/refine { eventId, prompt, selectedBlockId? } -> a proposal diff rendered through the same accept/reject path as eb-proposals.

items.element: 04-gapfill.html `.eb-answer` judge checkbox list; 'Select all 16' / 'Add someone new'
items.current: Five hardcoded contacts; checkboxes toggle but the count in the button is static and nothing is written.
items.needs: GET /api/crm/contacts?role=judge&event=<prevEventId> for the candidate list, then write chosen contact ids to the event's speakers field (the same field the Advanced Event screen uses). Also needs contact-create for 'Add someone new'.

items.current: Adding appends a rail row and flips the card to 'In use'; reorder swaps DOM siblings and re-appends canvas blocks; remove deletes both. All in-memory.
items.needs: Block membership + order persisted on the event, and the section/article scaffolding each block implies created server-side (this is the work the 'Created for you' notices describe). Locked 'Coming later' cards are deliberately inert.

items.current: Toggling swaps the tab strip for the sticky anchor nav and shows/hides `[data-eb-panel]` groups. Works fully client-side.
items.needs: Persist the chosen shape on the event and have the public template honour it. The rendering logic itself is front-end and can ship as-is.

items.current: Text is editable in the browser and the format bar is decorative. Edits are never saved and the 'Rewrite with AI' / 'Shorten' buttons do nothing.
items.needs: PATCH the corresponding event field per edited region (each editable needs a field binding), plus an AI rewrite endpoint for the two assistive format-bar actions. Undo needs a revision history.

items.current: Drop zones render; no file is read or stored.
items.needs: POST /api/media/upload -> media-library reference stored on the block/field. Should also allow picking an existing media-library item rather than only uploading.

items.current: Plain text inputs containing a human-readable item name and price.
items.needs: GET /api/catalogue/items with a picker bound to an item id (not a string), so the event's Buy Now / Book a table buttons resolve to real catalogue items and prices.

items.current: Static badges marking which fields the assistant wrote vs which were edited on the page; the SEO-title mismatch and its 'Fix it' button are hardcoded.
items.needs: Per-field provenance (who/what last wrote it: assistant, canvas edit, or form) stored with the event, plus a consistency check across related fields (title vs SEO title vs teaser) to generate these warnings.

items.current: Styled placeholder reading 'Map generated from the address'.
items.needs: Server-side geocode of the venue address returning map tiles or a static map image — the point being a structured address field instead of pasted embed code in the WYSIWYG.

items.element: 'Publish' / 'Save & publish' in the top bar; the 08 confirmation toast
items.current: Navigates to 08-published.html and shows a success toast unconditionally.
items.needs: Persist the event, run the publication rules (go-live date, access clearance, live flag) and return the public URL. The toast should reflect the real result, including validation failures.

items.current: Inert button.
items.needs: GET /api/events?clonable=1 for the picker, then a server-side deep copy of the event model plus its section scaffolding into a new draft.

SeatingPlanner.file: src/cc/patterns/EventPicker/ (screen 1, built) + src/prototypes/SeatingPlanner/ (screen 2 workspace shell, prototype)
SeatingPlanner.note: Control > CRM > Seating Planner. Screen 1 (event picker, TASK-342608) shipped as the EventPicker pattern. Screen 2 is the workspace shell — TASK-344753 — covering the event bar, seating plans row, toolbar, tables grid, seat panel and unassigned tray. That task is the shell + wiring only: each control's detail lives in its own sub-task and is marked up with [data-sp-action] + [data-sp-task], routed through one registry. A sub-task goes live by calling SeatingPlannerWorkspace.on('<action>', fn) — no refactor needed. Reads/writes SeatingPlan, Table and TableSeat (data model on the parent task); no new fields.

items.current: Rows are mock DOM; search filters already-loaded rows in the browser.
items.needs: GET /crm/events?status=live&sort=-startDate for the list; debounced GET /crm/events?q=<term> for search.

items.element: Pinned "Last used" row; the prototype keeps it in localStorage
items.current: Per-user last-used event is client-side only; the pattern deliberately leaves persistence to the host.
items.needs: Per-user preference read on module open and written on select. Named in the brief as a remaining item.

items.current: Static: picker over an empty workspace.
items.needs: Opening the module with no event chosen must show the picker and render nothing else until one is selected (Behaviour section of TASK-344753).

items.element: .sp-plan chips — name, table count, seated/capacity, fill bar
items.current: Two mock plans; chip selection swaps the visible tables client-side.
items.needs: GET the event's SeatingPlan rows with aggregate table/seat counts. Selecting a plan loads its Tables.

items.element: .sp-table cards — name, tier, sponsor, fill pill, seat dots
items.current: 36 mock cards (30 Main Ballroom + 6 Overflow). Fill pill and dots recompute client-side after an unseat.
items.needs: GET Tables for the selected plan with per-seat occupancy so the dots and fill pill derive from real TableSeat rows.

items.element: .sp-panel seat list — occupant, role tag, reorder, remove
items.current: Seats derived from mock dot data; reorder and remove work in the DOM and are lost on reload.
items.needs: Read/write TableSeat. Seat order is meaningful ("who sits next to whom") so reorder must persist an explicit index, not a sort. Remove clears the seat and returns the person to Unassigned.

items.element: .sp-panel Unassigned — role tag, name, company, live count, search
items.current: Seven mock people; search + count are live client-side; unseating appends to the tray.
items.needs: Attendees for the event with no TableSeat row. Owning sub-task TASK-351550.

items.current: Filters the grid to tables holding at least one empty seat. Fully working.
items.needs: Nothing server-side while the plan's tables are already loaded. Revisit only if table lists are paginated.

items.element: Every [data-sp-action] control: copy-plans 344756, add-table 344757, room-layout 344760, export 344761, table-edit 342307, table-delete 344758, assign-seat 342309
items.current: Render and are focusable; each announces its owning task via a toast instead of failing silently. Built so far: 342306 new-plan, 344754 plan-edit, 344755 plan-delete, 344756 copy-plans, 344757 add-table, 342307 table-edit.
items.needs: One sub-task each. Register a handler with SeatingPlannerWorkspace.on(action, fn) and the control goes live — the shell needs no change.

items.element: Seat rows and tray rows carry draggable="true"; no drop handling
items.current: Drag is not implemented. The per-seat Assign action is the path shown.
items.needs: TASK-344759. Recommendation from this build: make Assign the canonical path on every viewport and treat drag as a desktop accelerator — HTML5 drag does not work on touch and keyboard users cannot drag, so the tap/click path is required regardless.

items.current: TASK-342307 NAMES THE SET: Standard / Gold / Silver / Bronze / VIP / Head table / Sponsor, "shown as a colour on the plan". Note Premium (used in the earlier build) is NOT in that list — migrated to Gold. Interim mapping: the five ranked tiers use an ordered ramp derived from ONE token (--ai-border-primary mixed toward the paper), Sponsor reuses the gold that already means sponsorship on the card (the star), Standard is unmarked, and the tier LABEL always renders so tier is never colour-only.
items.needs: TASK-342308 decides the real colours, and three questions come with it. (1) Gold/Silver/Bronze are named BY colour, so literal metallics mean 3+ new DS tokens. (2) A table card would then carry three colour systems at once — 7 tier colours, 6 role colours on the seat dots, 3 fill states — which is what the shell deliberately simplified. (3) VIP and Sponsor are BOTH tier values and role values, so the same word can mean two things in two colours on one card; Sponsor is also a separate field on the table form, so Type=Sponsor with an empty Sponsor field is currently undefined.

items.current: Modal validates the two required fields and the 6–12 seats bound, then creates the plan chip and generates its table cards entirely in the DOM. Lost on reload. Registers itself on the shell via SeatingPlannerWorkspace.on('new-plan', …) — the shell was not modified.
items.needs: POST a SeatingPlan with { name (required), room, tables (required), seatsPerTable (default 10, bounded 6–12), tableShape (Round|Square) } and an FK to the selected Event; generate Table + TableSeat rows server-side; return the created plan so the plans row and grid re-read rather than being built client-side. Server must re-validate — the client bound is a convenience, not a guarantee.

items.element: Table shape (Round / Square) — set at generation time in the New plan popup
items.current: Captured on the plan and echoed in the confirmation toast, but nothing renders shape: the tables grid shows no shape indicator, and TASK-344753's table cards have no shape affordance.
items.needs: Decide whether shape is display-only metadata or should render on the table card / in the Room layout view (TASK-344760). Raised by this build — the shell predates the field.

items.current: Opens from a chip's ✎ pre-filled from THAT chip (the shell passes the clicked control through as ctx.trigger). Saving renames the chip, updates its room, rebuilds the label the toolbar reads, and refreshes the action buttons' aria-labels. DOM-only, lost on reload.
items.needs: PATCH the SeatingPlan record with { name (required), room }. Renaming must NOT touch the plan's Tables or TableSeats — verified in the prototype: a rename leaves all 30 tables and the open seat panel intact. Re-read the plans row after saving rather than patching the DOM.

items.current: alertdialog on a chip's ✕, opened from the clicked chip. Copy is data-driven — table and seated counts are read off the DOM, and the people clause is dropped when nobody is seated. Confirming removes the chip and its table cards, injects every returned occupant into the Unassigned tray, and if the deleted plan was open, selects the next remaining plan (or folds the workspace away and restores the "No plans yet" hint when none are left). Esc cancels. DOM-only.
items.needs: Delete the SeatingPlan plus its Table and TableSeat rows in ONE transaction and return the occupants to the event pool. A partial failure must not leave people unassigned from a plan that still exists. Re-read the plans row and the Unassigned pool after deleting rather than patching the DOM. The counts in the dialog must come from the server, not the client, so a stale page can't understate what is about to be destroyed.

items.element: Copy plans to event — copyplans-*.html + SeatingPlannerCopyPlans.js
items.current: Destination list reuses screen 1's Event Picker rows (.sp-event) and predictive search; the current event is excluded so a plan can't be copied onto itself. Intro copy is data-driven (plan count + source event name read off the page). Selecting a destination bumps that row's plan count and toasts what was copied. DOM-only.
items.needs: Insert cloned SeatingPlan + Table rows under the target Event with TableSeat occupants left EMPTY — tables, capacities, types and sponsors carried, attendees not. Clone in ONE transaction so a failure can't leave half a layout. Destination list is GET /crm/events excluding the current event, with a debounced ?q= search.

items.element: Destination rows showing an existing plan count (e.g. "1 plan")
items.current: Copy is INSERT, not replace: copying 2 plans into an event that already has 1 leaves it with 3. The prototype makes this visible by showing each destination's current plan count and incrementing it, but nothing warns before the fact.
items.needs: Confirm the intended semantics. If append is right, consider naming clones to avoid two plans called "Main Ballroom" in one event. If replace is ever wanted it needs its own confirmation, since it would destroy existing seating. Raised by this build — the brief says "insert" but doesn't cover the collision case.

items.current: No popup. Appends a card with the next table number, the plan's default seat count (data-sp-plan-seats, set when the plan was created), every seat empty; recomputes the plan chip and toolbar count, and opens the new table so its empty seat list is on screen.
items.needs: Insert a Table plus its empty TableSeat rows under the plan. Assign the table number and sort order SERVER-SIDE — computing either on the client races other editors. Note the number must be max(existing)+1, not count+1: after deleting Table 3 of 5, count+1 would mint a second Table 5. Seat count comes from the PLAN default, not from the last table, since individual tables can have been changed.

items.element: Plan chip summary "N tables · X/Y seated · Z free" + its fill bar
items.current: BUG FOUND AND FIXED during TASK-344757: the chip was written once and never recomputed, so the summary went stale the moment anyone was unseated — the plan summary silently lied. syncPlanChip() now recomputes it from the plan's tables and is called on unseat and on add-table; it is published on the shell API for later sub-tasks that add or remove tables.
items.needs: Nothing server-side while a plan's tables are all loaded — the recompute is client-side. Any sub-task that changes table or seat counts must call SeatingPlannerWorkspace.syncPlanChip(planKey), or derive the summary from the server response.

items.element: Table form, New / Edit (TASK-342307) — tableform-*.html + SeatingPlannerTableForm.js
items.current: Opens pre-filled from a table's edit action. Name (required), tier (the 7 named values), sponsor via account lookup with predictive search, host, capacity, shape. Saving rewrites the card's name, tier class + label, sponsor line, dots, count and fill pill, then resyncs the plan chip. DOM-only.
items.needs: Table row with FKs — Type → Table Type lookup, Sponsor → Account — plus a sort order. Accounts list is GET /crm/accounts?q=. Capacity changes must add/remove TableSeat rows and unassign the surplus in the SAME transaction.

items.current: The note states current occupancy and escalates to a warning naming exactly how many people will be displaced before you save. On save the surplus is taken from the HIGHEST-numbered seats and returned to Unassigned; increasing capacity appends empty seats. Verified 10→7 returned 3, and 7→12 added 5 empty.
items.needs: Server must decide and record WHICH occupants are displaced. Taking the last seats is the only sensible automatic rule, but seat order is meaningful here ("who sits next to whom"), so confirm with the spec team whether the user should choose instead of the system picking. Unassign in the same transaction as the seat removal.

items.element: "New table" mode of the table form (tableform-new.html)
items.current: The form supports a New mode and it is captured, but NOTHING opens it: TASK-344757's Add table button creates a table instantly from the plan defaults, with no form.
items.needs: Resolve the overlap between the two briefs. 344757 says Add table adds straight away; 342307 is titled "New / Edit Table form". Either Add table should open this form pre-filled with the defaults, or the New mode is dead and should be dropped. Raised by this build.
